Compare the action sheet panel with the page behind it in Light and Dark.
Open the Rename dialog from the sheet and compare its panel background.

Tap Dark.
Read the bold option names and the grey description lines.
Compare how readable the grey text is with Expected.

steps: Open Settings > Device > Appearance.
Look at the thin lines between the System, Light and Dark rows.
Switch Light and Dark and compare the line strength.
Compare the lines with Expected (subtle, not heavy).

Open Device > Accent Color.
Tap a colour such as Blue or Rose.
Check that the selected accent shows on the selected mark and on buttons, and that its text is readable.

S6.06.needs: a phone you can turn offline
S6.06.note: The labels are accessibility labels; the visible text was not confirmed.
steps: Turn off Wi-Fi and mobile data on the phone.
Send a chat message.
Look for the status text under the message (Message queued offline or Message failed to send).
Compare the success, warning and error colours with Expected in Light and Dark.
S6.06.where: Message status text: a message that is queued offline or fails to send in the chat

S6.07.note: The font declarations are in apps/mobile/tailwind.config.js and apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx; the editorial face was not confirmed in any screen.

Open a chat and read the reply text.
Compare the font look with Expected (one sans, one editorial, one monospace).

steps: Open Settings > Device > Appearance.
Compare the size and weight of the screen title with the Theme heading.
Open another settings screen, such as Accent Color, and compare the title style.
Check the headings match across screens.

S6.09.needs: a phone where you can change text size
S6.09.note: No in-app text-size setting was found; the code reads the device font scale (apps/mobile/src/shared/components/TextScaleBoundary.tsx).

Change the phone's text size in the phone's own settings.
Reopen the app and compare the body text size.
S6.09.where: Body text size: no in-app text-size control was found; device text size changes app text

steps: Open Settings > Device > Appearance.
Read the grey line under Light: Bright neutral interface.
Compare its size with the bold option name above it.
Check it is at least as large as 12 px and easy to read.
S6.10.where: Small caption text: the grey description line under each Appearance option

S6.11.note: The monospace family is declared in apps/mobile/tailwind.config.js; the code block copy control was not matched to a visible label.
steps: Ask the chat for a short code sample.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Compare the code text with the body text around it.
Check the code uses a monospace face and a different size.
S6.11.where: Code text in a chat reply: any reply that contains a code block

steps: Ask the chat a question that gets a multi-line answer.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Look at the gap between lines in one paragraph.
Compare the line spacing with Expected.
S6.12.where: Line spacing in a chat reply that has several lines

steps: Ask the chat for a reply with three or more paragraphs.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Measure the gap between two paragraphs by eye.
Check the gap is the same between every pair.
S6.13.where: Paragraph gaps in a chat reply with several paragraphs

steps: Ask the chat for a nested bullet list.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Look at the indent of the first and second levels.
Check each level indents by the same step.
S6.14.where: Bullet-list indentation in a chat reply

S6.15.note: The copy control label for code blocks was not confirmed.
steps: Ask the chat for a short code sample.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Look at the space between the code text and the edge of its box.
Compare the padding on the top, bottom and sides.
S6.15.where: Padding inside a code block in a chat reply

steps: Ask the chat for a small table, such as three columns and three rows.
Wait for the reply to finish.
Look at the space inside each cell.
Compare the padding across cells.
S6.16.where: Table cell padding in a chat reply that contains a table

steps: Send a first message in a chat and wait for the reply.
Send a second message.
Measure the gap between the turns.
Check it matches the gap used between other turns.
S6.17.where: Space between two chat turns (one question and one reply, then the next question)

S6.18.note: How the action row is opened was not confirmed in the code.
steps: Send a message and wait for the reply.
Look at the action row below the reply.
Compare the gap between the reply text and the action row with Expected.
Check the row sits the same distance below each reply.
S6.18.where: Chat: under an AI reply, its action row (Good response, Bad response, Copy Message)

S6.19.note: No fixed visible words for the composer were found outside the placeholder cases.

Watch the toast slide in and out and note it is quick, not slow.

S6.31.needs: a phone or simulator where the Reduce Motion setting can be changed
S6.31.note: No in-app control exists for reduced motion; only the OS setting is read (useReduceMotion.ts). The OfflineBanner cited in the plan does not loop, so it was not used as an example.
steps: On the phone or simulator, turn on the system Reduce Motion setting (iOS path: Settings > Accessibility > Motion > Reduce Motion; this path is the phone's own and is not in the repo).
Open AGI Mobile and go to a chat where the loading spinner shows (apps/mobile/components/ui/LoadingIndicator.tsx uses a spinning AgiMark).
Look at the spinner and any looping mark: it should stop or be replaced by a gentle change.
Compare with the rule in apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/useReduceMotion.ts and the check in apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/__tests__/accessibilityPreferenceCoverage.test.ts.
S6.31.where: Reduce Motion is a phone setting outside the app, read by the app at startup and live. There is no in-app switch in apps/mobile.

S6.32.needs: a Mac or phone where the system light or dark setting can be changed
S6.32.note: Cloud and Local modes store their theme choice separately (appearance/index.tsx), so check the choice in the mode you are using. Whether code blocks follow the theme was not verified in code.
steps: Sign in and tap Open menu to open the side drawer, then tap Settings.
Under the Device group, tap Appearance.
Tap Dark and look at the whole app, including code blocks in a chat, for a dark background.
Tap Light, then System, and check the app follows the device's light or dark setting.
S6.32.where: Drawer > Settings > Device > Appearance, then choose System, Light or Dark.

S6.33.needs: a phone or simulator where the system contrast setting can be changed
S6.33.note: The code is in apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/useSystemHighContrast.ts; the high-contrast palette is in apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/tokens.ts (highContrastColors). The device menu path is the phone's own, so confirm it on the device.
steps: On the phone, turn on the high-contrast setting (iOS: the Darker Colors setting, which the code reads as isDarkerSystemColorsEnabled; Android: the high text contrast setting, read as isHighTextContrastEnabled). These device paths are not in the repo.
Open AGI Mobile and check text and borders look stronger.
Check the accent colour is replaced by neutral colours, as in apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/useTheme.ts (accent is null when high contrast is on).
S6.33.where: Phone setting outside the app: high contrast is read from the system. There is no in-app switch.

S6.34.note: Focus and hover states are not verified in the code on this screen; the disabled example was not located. The plan's pressable-box.tsx path is now PressableBox.tsx.
steps: Sign in, tap Open menu, then Settings, then Appearance.
Press and hold the System row and check it shows a pressed state.
Release and check the row you picked now shows a check mark and is marked selected.
Look for a disabled state on a greyed-out control elsewhere, and compare with the pressed and selected states in apps/mobile/components/ui/PressableBox.tsx.
S6.34.where: Drawer > Settings > Device > Appearance (selected row shows a check mark; pressing a row shows a pressed state).

S6.35.needs: a phone or simulator with the app installed

Look at the brand symbol at the top of the About screen (apps/mobile/app/(app)/about.tsx).
